methodologyNotes: Covers force-feedback sim racing wheel bases sold to consumers at a published US MSRP, including the direct-drive, belt-driven, and gear-driven bases that form the core of a sim racing wheel. Excludes standalone wheel rims sold without a base, non-force-feedback (spring/rubber-band) wheels, and full cockpits or rigs. Price is US MSRP for the base as configured, in USD; where a model ships only as a bundle, price is the typical bundle MSRP and wheelRimIncluded is true. driveType is one of direct-drive, belt-driven, or gear-driven. peakTorqueNm is the manufacturer-rated peak force-feedback torque in newton-metres (Nm). holdingTorqueNm is the rated continuous/holding torque in Nm; null if not disclosed. platformCompat is the set of natively supported platforms, one of: PC, PC+PlayStation, PC+Xbox, or PC+PlayStation+Xbox. maxRotationDeg is the maximum steering rotation in degrees, or the string "unlimited" for mechanically unbounded direct-drive bases. wheelRimIncluded is a boolean: true if a wheel rim ships with the base. quickReleaseStandard is the name of the wheel-side quick-release standard (e.g. Fanatec QR2, MOZA, Simucube SQR, 70mm bolt-on). mountingOptions is one of: desk-clamp, bolt-mount, or both. connectionType is the host connection, one of USB-C or USB-B. weightKg is the wheel base weight in kilograms.

products.name: MOZA R12
products.priceNote: US MSRP/typical price. GigaParts (US retailer, SKU JS0645, "MOZA RACING RS081 R12 V2 Direct Drive Wheel Base - 12Nm Torque") lists "Regular Price: $429.00" (current price $399.00 after a "$30.00 Instant Rebate (Exp. 07-15-2026)"); the directdrivewheels.com review corroborates "$429". MOZA's own US store shows a mid-year-sale price of $399.00 USD against a $469.00 USD regular-price anchor.
products.provenance: The official MOZA Racing US store page confirms the exact model ("MOZA R12 V2 Direct Drive Wheel Base") and its spec sheet: FFB Drive System Direct Drive, Peak Torque 12 N·m, Platform PC, Weight 7.5 kg, Fixing Method 4-hole bottom mount with Desk Clamp Optional, and a base-only "What's in box" (no wheel rim). GigaParts (US retailer, SKU JS0645) corroborates the identical spec table and lists a regular price of $429.00 (instant-rebate price $399.00, exp. 07-15-2026), while the directdrivewheels.com review confirms the "standard Moza quick release", PC-only native platform (Xbox only via a licensed ESX rim, no PlayStation), and June 2023 as the R12's ship date. maxRotationDeg is recorded as "unlimited" per methodology since the R12 is a mechanically unbounded direct-drive base (GigaParts spec: "Max Wheel Rotation: Limitless"; MOZA lists a 90~2700° software-adjustable range); holding torque and the USB connector type (USB-C vs USB-B) are not disclosed on any fetched page, so both are null.

products.name: Fanatec ClubSport DD+

The 6Sigma Sim Racing retailer page corroborates the identical SKU (CS_DD+_US) and $899.99 price, and additionally lists the manufacturer spec-sheet "Product Weight 10,6 kg" (10.6 kg), Direct Drive, 18Nm, up-to-2520 rotation, and Fanatec QR2. products.name: Logitech G RS50
products.priceNote: US MSRP $349.99 for the standalone RS50 wheelbase (PC configuration). Logitech's official launch blog lists "RS50 Wheelbase (PC): $349.99 / €299.99"; the Boosted Media review corroborates verbatim: "At US$349.99 for the standalone 8Nm wheelbase" and "At $349.99 USD, the RS50 wheelbase delivers a solid 8Nm of torque." Higher configs ($449.99 PlayStation/PC base; $699.99 System) are not used since the base standalone MSRP is the convention.
products.provenance: Logitech's official launch blog (logitech.com, dated Sept 17 2025) confirms the RS50 Base is a direct-drive wheelbase delivering "up to 8Nm of peak torque" with TRUEFORCE and a slip-ring giving "up to 2700 degrees of rotation," and lists the PC wheelbase MSRP as "RS50 Wheelbase (PC): $349.99," available globally Sept 17 2025. Boosted Media's detailed review corroborates the exact model ("Logitech G RS50 Direct Drive Wheelbase") and price ("US$349.99 for the standalone 8Nm wheelbase"), and notes bottom bolt-mount plus table-clamp mounting. Amazon's listing (Model Number 941-000264, "Logitech G RS50") independently confirms model identity, 8 Nm direct drive, USB connectivity, and both "table clamp" and "racing seat mounting hardware" — verifying this is the RS50, not the 11Nm G PRO or another sibling.

products.name: Thrustmaster T818
products.priceNote: US MSRP $649.99. Listed verbatim as "T818 BLACK EDITION $649.99" on Thrustmaster's official US store (eshop.thrustmaster.com) and as "$649.99 at Thrustmaster US" in the Windows Central review (published 2023-04-29). The same review also references a "$750 MSRP" figure in its body text, but the current manufacturer US store price and the review's own buy box both list $649.99.
products.provenance: The Thrustmaster US product page (the /products/t818/ URL redirects to "T818 Black Edition", the current V2 revision of the T818) confirms Direct Drive technology, a constant 10 N·m torque with no saturation, 5 kg weight, PC-only platform, an aeronautical-grade Quick Release wheel mount, and both cockpit (4 bolt points) and desk (clamp kit) mounting, with box contents that include no wheel rim. Amazon's listing confirms the exact identity "Thrustmaster T818 Servo Base" (item model 2960877, Windows, release date August 1, 2023), and the dated Windows Central review (2023-04-29) corroborates the specs — up to 10 Nm, 5 kg, exclusively PC, USB-C-to-USB-A cable, no wheel rims included — and lists the price as "$649.99 at Thrustmaster US". Model identity verified: this is the T818 direct-drive servo base sold base-only (no rim), not the T598 sibling nor a wheel bundle.

SimRaceBlog's dated 7 January 2024 hands-on review independently corroborates the same Invicta 27Nm model's 11.3kg weight, 27Nm torque, direct-drive design, and USB-C PC connection.
